content: Regret never walks in front of the deed; it always follows in the shadows.
author: Japanese Proverbs
sourceWork: Koukai saki ni tatazu (後悔先に立たず)
explanation: Impulse is loud and intoxicating; it blinds us with urgency. Regret, however, never shows up during the temptation—it waits quietly behind the curtain until the damage is done. Wisdom is the discipline of consulting the consequences before taking the step.
practicalInsight: Whenever anger or instant gratification urges you to send an emotional message today, pause for twenty minutes and visualize tomorrow morning.
reflectionPrompt: What habitual impulse are you tempted to indulge, knowing full well the bitter taste of regret that always follows?
